findings.where: Article specimen: the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' and the closing paragraph's 'world's best PPP law' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: These two apostrophes are straight typewriter marks. Every other quote mark in the article is a curly typographer's mark: “What is the best…”, ‘chapter topics’, ‘Abundance’. The worst case is the 44 px title, where the straight tick is easy to see.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder, who want this direction to have a legal journal's editorial gravitas. A reader at a development bank, used to well-set reports, sees mixed quote marks as careless setting. Angélique will copy this specimen as the model for future articles.

findings.where: Photo captions: the hero portrait's 'Placeholder…' caption (right-aligned under the frame on desktop, centred under the photo on phone) and the article photo's caption (left-aligned)
findings.fault: The page has two captions, and they are aligned three different ways. The hero caption is right-aligned on desktop and centred on phone. The article caption is left-aligned on the text column, as is every other line of text on the sheet.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who is judging whether this look gives Angélique one set of rules she can reuse. Captions with no single alignment make the type system look improvised, and they break the left edge that every other line on the sheet keeps.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the easing-curve diagram box (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The diagram's hairline box starts about 7 px to the right of the column's left edge. Its caption below and every other block in the specimen column start exactly on that edge. The hairline makes the step easy to see.
findings.who_objects: The founder, or any designer reviewing the tile. This direction's one borrowed detail is a precise document edge drawn in hairlines, so a hairline box slightly off the column edge looks like a setting slip.
